content.title: The Voice's Top 4 Artists Revealed: Who Got Voted to Season 29's Finale
content.text: It all comes down to this. The hard work, the long hours, the talent and the dreaming. Four incredible singers vying to be the champion of The Voice Season 29. They can rely on their Coaches Kelly Clarkson, John Legend, and Adam Levine for expert guidance, but not for help in the competition phase, as audience votes now determine the outcome. And they're going up against the best of the best.How to WatchThese Artists sang their hearts out for the in-studio audience voters during the Semi-Finals of The Voice: Battle of Champions and were the top picks from their three teams. One is a season-long frontrunner with a booming sound comparable to the divas of the past: Whitney Houston and Aretha Franklin are just some of the women she's capably covered. Another is an alt teen in a unique lane all her own. The youngest is the comeback kid, who failed to make it past the Blind Auditions just a season ago. Finally, the lone male Finalist brings a singer-songwriter vibe to the stage that could give him the edge.RELATED: The Voice: Battle of Champions Has a Totally New Voting Format: Here's How It WorkWith Team Kelly getting two entries into the Finals, these are the Top 4 Artists heading into Tuesday night's Finale for The Voice: Battle of Champions.Lucas West — Team LegendWest showed off every facet of his voice singing Paul McCartney's "Maybe I'm Amazed." In fact, his Coach was...amazed! “I love this song for Lucas. It’s big, it’s urgent, it’s passionate, it allows him to wail and hit those high notes,” said Legend.For his performance, West accompanied himself on the piano and was backed by a choir, creating a sound so full that Clarkson told him he could "crush" a stadium gig. Now, he's one step closer to making that happen.RELATED: The Voice Season 29: The Ultimate Episode-by-Episode Guide for Super FansAlexia Jayy — Team AdamFor her performance, Jayy chose “I Never Loved a Man (The Way I Love You)” by Aretha Franklin, a song Clarkson revealed she loves so much that she doesn't like to hear other people singing it. Jayy, however, "can sing it any damn day," according to Clarkson.As for Levine, he couldn't resist gushing about his Season 29 Finalist. "Alexia has a tone that is masterful, it’s soulful, she is one of the best singers I have ever heard in my life," he said during rehearsals. "You don’t just love singing. It is in your DNA and in your bones."Mikenley Brown — Team KellyEveryone agreed that Brown gave her best performance to date singing “I’m Not the Only One” by Sam Smith, speculating that in front of a crowd of other singers, she knew she'd have to bring her A-game and stepped it up."Believability is a huge thing for me. A lot of people come out here and sing great songs but I don’t buy it. And I buy it from you," said Clarkson, praising Brown for making her feel it. “I am beaming over here ... I think you might’ve snuck up on people,” added Legend.RELATED: NBA Legend Jimmy Butler Has Joined The Voice: Battle of Champions: "Go Coaches!"Liv Ciara — Team Kelly Equally competitive was Ciara, the ultimate dark horse. "It's crazy to me that someone with her gift would not get four chair turns, let alone none," remarked Clarkson, referring to Ciara's Blind Audition during Season 28. Singing a stripped-down version of "What a Feeling" by Irene Cara, however, Ciara left no doubt that she belonged on The Voice stage."She’s a beast. She is 16 and she wants that crown, and she is coming for it," declared Clarkson. "I did not know until this day that she might win this show," added Legend, with Levine agreeing that it was her "breakout moment" when she "slid into the front."The two-hour episode for The Voice Season 29 Finale airs on Tuesday, April 14 at 9/8c on NBC and next day on Peacock. Tune in to find out who's been voted as the next winner of The Voice!
